Two relations are available.

  corpus      one row per document in the working sample, WITH the text.
  corpus_meta one row per document in the whole corpus, WITHOUT the text.

Columns (identical in both, except `text`, which only `corpus` has):
  id                    document identifier
  text                  document text (corpus only)
  url, domain           source URL and its host
  dump, date            crawl the document came from, and its timestamp
  language              language label assigned by the corpus pipeline
  language_score        the pipeline's confidence in that label
  minhash_cluster_size  size of the near-duplicate cluster the document
                        represented before deduplication (1 = unique)
  fasttext, langdetect  labels from two independent off-the-shelf language
                        identifiers, shipped with the corpus release
  lingua_top            top language from a third identifier, which reports
                        a distribution over languages within the document
  lingua_top_p          that identifier's proportion for lingua_top
  n_bad_words           number of profanity-list matches recorded by the
                        corpus release
  n_chars, n_words, n_lines  document size
Raw pipeline fields `top_langs` (JSON) and `lingua` (list of
(language, proportion) pairs, as text) are also available on both
relations if you want the full distributions.

input.description: A systematic subset of documents are Czech-language or heavily Czech/Slovak code-switched, not clean Slovak, yet are labelled language='slk' with high language_score. This mostly comes from (a) Slovak e-commerce sites that paste Czech-language product descriptions/reviews verbatim from shared CZ/SK catalogs and (b) cz.pinterest.com / forum pages whose captions and comments mix Czech and Slovak. Because Czech and Slovak are highly mutually intelligible, the pipeline's own LID and all three shipped auxiliary LIDs (fasttext, langdetect, lingua) confidently but wrongly agree that many such documents are Slovak, and even when they agree the document is Czech, the corpus still ships it labelled slk.
input.evidence: Inspected 22 documents where all three auxiliary LIDs (fasttext, langdetect, lingua_top) independently label the text 'cs' while the corpus's own pipeline still labels it 'slk' (seeds 2 and 3). About 16/22 clearly contained substantial or dominant Czech-language text: pure-Czech pages crawled from .cz domains (ciirc.cvut.cz academic page, dg-shop.cz, zks-shop.cz, stoklasa-sk.sk, monelli.cz), and, more frequently, nominally-Slovak e-shops (bonami.sk, svet-kupelne.sk, krasnadoma.sk, b2b.agfoods.sk, kuchynsky-drez.sk) and cz.pinterest.com boards whose product/recipe text is untranslated Czech pasted alongside Slovak site chrome. Counter-evidence: 6/22 were false positives where the text was actually fully idiomatic Slovak (e.g. bezkempu.cz camping listing, modrykonik.sk forum posts, a car-brand name list) that all three external LIDs misjudged as Czech, presumably because Slovak dialectal/colloquial text and short brand-name lists are hard to distinguish from Czech. Prevalence of the strict triple-agreement selector is 44,251/26,470,482 = 0.17% of the full corpus; loosening to fasttext='cs' alone matches 412,528 (1.6%) but with visibly lower precision on manual inspection.
input.likely_false_positives: Genuinely Slovak documents (colloquial forum speech, short lists of proper nouns/brand names, or terse product listings) that confuse all three external language identifiers into guessing Czech even though the corpus's own slk label is correct.
input.assertion: Documents where fasttext, langdetect and lingua all independently agree the text is Czech should not be shipped under a pure-Slovak language label without at least a code-switch/contamination flag.

input.description: A massive programmatic content-farm/doorway-page network hosted on Google Firebase's free static hosting (*.firebaseapp.com and *.web.app subdomains) accounts for over 5% of the entire corpus. Each domain is auto-named from a finance/scam keyword template (Slovak: akoinvestovat-, akozbohatnut-, pracovnemiesta-, investicie-, predajakcii-, nakupzlata-, dane-, plat-, podnikanie-; Swedish: kopavguld-, hurman-, enklapengar-, investerarpengar-, skatter-, valuta-, lon-, jobb-) plus a random alphanumeric suffix, with URLs of the form /<digits>/<digits>.html. The page text is not authored prose but a concatenation of unrelated scraped fragments (finance tips, celebrity trivia, government-office instructions, product ads, forum snippets) frequently spanning several languages within a single document (Slovak, Czech, Portuguese, Slovenian, Serbo-Croatian, Swedish...). Despite this, the pipeline's own language classifier assigns these documents 'slk' with very high confidence (often >0.99) and the shipped fasttext/langdetect/lingua identifiers usually agree on 'sk', apparently because the Slovak-language fragment(s) embedded in the stitched page dominate surface statistics.
input.evidence: Inspected 27 documents matching this selector across three random samples (seeds 21, 99, plus 2 via inspect_document for full text): 27/27 showed the same signature — incoherent concatenation of scraped, topically-unrelated fragments, often multi-language within one document, hosted on a freshly-suffixed keyword-themed Firebase subdomain, with the numeric-path URL pattern. domain_stats/aggregate confirm 2,851 distinct such domains in the corpus, each contributing roughly 2,000-2,600 documents (share_of_domain effectively 1.0, i.e. every document these domains contribute matches), which is consistent with automated bulk generation rather than organic sites. Full-text inspection of two documents showed paragraph-by-paragraph language switching (Slovak paragraph, then Portuguese pesticide-ad paragraph, then Serbian public-transport-card instructions, then Czech privacy-policy boilerplate) with no topical or grammatical coherence between paragraphs — this is not translated or code-switched natural text but mechanically concatenated scrape output. Prevalence: 1,408,437 / 26,470,482 = 5.32% of the full corpus, making it likely the single largest coherent quality defect found in this audit. No counter-examples (legitimate firebaseapp.com/web.app sites) were found in any of the three samples or in a targeted check of the 50 most frequent such domains, all of which fit the keyword+suffix naming template.
input.likely_false_positives: A legitimate small business or personal project hosted on Firebase's free tier with organically-written Slovak content would also match this domain pattern; none were observed in ~30 inspected documents, but the selector cannot distinguish them from the spam network by domain alone.
input.assertion: Documents from *.firebaseapp.com / *.web.app domains matching the finance-keyword-plus-random-suffix naming template should be excluded from a corpus claiming to be curated, deduplicated, natural Slovak text.

## Summary

I audited the Slovak (`slk_Latn`) slice of this web corpus (26.47M documents in `corpus_meta`, 2.03M with text in `corpus`) using aggregate queries, targeted sampling, and manual inspection (used ~163 of 300 inspection budget). Three systematic, quantified defects were found and recorded via `save_finding`; several other hypotheses were tested and rejected.

### Findings recorded

1. **`firebase_webapp_content_farm`** — **5.32% of the corpus (1,408,437 docs)**. A programmatic content-farm/doorway-page network on Google Firebase free hosting (`*.firebaseapp.com`, `*.web.app`), 2,851 distinct auto-named domains (finance-scam keyword + random suffix, in Slovak *and* Swedish), each page a mechanical concatenation of unrelated scraped fragments, often spanning several languages/scripts within one document. The corpus's own LID confidently (often >0.99) mislabels these as clean `slk`. This is the single largest defect found — confirmed in 27/27 inspected documents. Confined entirely to 2022–2023 crawls.

2. **`adult_spam_farm_wordsalad`** — **0.39% of the corpus (102,474 docs)**, selector `n_bad_words >= 3`. A distinct network of throwaway adult-content SEO domains producing grammatically incoherent keyword-stuffed "Slovak" text (word-salad, not prose), confirmed in 25/25 sampled documents, with dozens of single-purpose domains where 75–92% of all their documents match. Verified `n_bad_words=1` (excluded) is mostly ordinary legitimate content, confirming the threshold separates spam from incidental profanity.

3. **`czech_slovak_code_switched_docs`** — **0.17% of the corpus (44,251 docs)**, selector: all three shipped auxiliary LIDs (fasttext, langdetect, lingua) agree the text is Czech. Mostly Slovak e-shops/Pinterest boards pasting untranslated Czech catalog/recipe text, plus some pure-Czech pages. Precision ~0.7 — genuine false positives exist (idiomatic Slovak text that fools all three external LIDs), documented honestly.

Overlap between the three selectors is small (checked pairwise), confirming they capture largely distinct populations.

### Hypotheses tested and rejected/set aside
- **Large minhash-cluster "representative" documents as boilerplate/widget contamination** (cookie banners, loan-ad widgets, login walls shared across many sites): real pattern, confirmed via `minhash_cluster_size > 10000` samples, but prevalence is tiny (489 docs, 0.0018%) and precision only ~60–70% (many high-cluster docs are legitimate short e-commerce content) — not filed as it's weak/low-materiality next to the three above.
- **Short documents (`n_words < 60`, 5.9% of corpus)** as an inherent quality defect: sampling showed these are mostly ordinary, legitimate short e-commerce product listings — normal web diversity, not a systematic labelling/quality failure.
- **CJK/Cyrillic script leakage** (regex sweep): confirms the firebase-farm phenomenon extends in kind to a few other domains, but is largely the same underlying phenomenon already captured by finding #1; not filed separately to avoid double-counting one phenomenon.
- **`n_bad_words = 1`** as a spam indicator: rejected — mostly normal content (news, health forums) that merely mentions a sensitive topic once.

### What I'd investigate next with more budget
- Whether the Firebase content-farm network has sibling clusters on other free-hosting platforms (`.pages.dev`, `.netlify.app`, `.github.io`) that a domain-only selector would miss.
- A text-based (not domain-based) detector for the content-farm phenomenon, e.g. paragraph-to-paragraph language-switching, to catch spam pages hosted on ordinary-looking domains (a few were spotted: `itam.ws`, `uvernabyvanie.sbs`, `mazorhomes.com`).
- Precision refinement of the Czech/Slovak code-switch selector, e.g. weighting by `lingua_top_p` or document length, to reduce the false-positive rate on genuinely Slovak dialectal/short text.
- Whether `minhash_cluster_size` correlates with crawl date in a way that shows the corpus is accumulating near-duplicate homepage snapshots faster than genuine content over time.
